rules: Import `ruststream_rumqttc::prelude::*` at a mount site, which brings the core prelude, the descriptors and the policy as `Publish`; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` alone (Prelude page).
Subscribe with `MqttTopic` for one topic and `MqttFilter` for a filter with `+` or `#`; a bare `#[subscriber("devices/dev42/telemetry")]` is an `MqttTopic` with the defaults (Subscriptions page).
Spread a topic over replicas with `.shared("group")` on the descriptor, so the server hands each message to one member of the share group (shared page).
Name where an `MqttFilter` registration's retry copies go with `.out_retry(Publish::default()).to("topic")`, or per delivery with a transform declaring `Destination = Names` (out_retry page).
Mount a `&[T]` handler with `.batch(n)` at the mount site; the crate fills each batch on the client and closes it at `n` deliveries or 20 ms after its first one (Batches page).

Declare the QoS and retain flag once with `Publish::default().qos(..).retain(..)` at the mount site, and change one message with the `.qos(..)` and `.retain(..)` steps of `MqttPublishSteps` (MqttPublishSteps page).
Bound a slot `Out<impl Publisher<Options = MqttPublishOptions>, Marker>` and import this crate's prelude only in a handler body that takes the `qos` or `retain` step (MqttPublishSteps page).
Set the `content-type` header with a publish transform at the mount site where peers read the MQTT 5 content type and payload format indicator (Headers page).
Return `HandlerOutcome::retry_after(delay)` to retry within the session; `retry()` leaves a QoS 1/2 delivery unacknowledged until a persistent session resumes (retry_after and retry pages).
Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(topic)` after `include`, with a dead-letter topic that matches no filter the service reads (Retries and Dead letters pages).
Keep a session across restarts with `MqttBroker::clean_start(false)` and a `session_expiry`, so the server queues what arrives while the service is away (Session page).

Choose what a lost connection does with `MqttBroker::reconnect(Reconnect::..)`: `automatic(AutoReconnect)` is the default, `never()` ends every stream, `custom(reconnector)` runs a `Reconnector` of the service's own (Reconnect page).
Answer a request on its response topic with a reply transform that reads `reply-to` and copies `correlation-id`, declaring `Destination = Names` (Responders page).
Test a service by handing the app `main` runs to `TestApp::start` with the `testing` feature and addressing the broker as `tb.broker::<MqttBroker>()` (Testing page).
Run the same test body against a running MQTT server with `TestApp::start_live` for a persistent session, the last will and the receive window (Live page).
Keep one key's messages in order with `workers(n, by_key)`; the publisher sets `PARTITION_KEY_HEADER` (`partition-key`) on each message, as a user property (Lanes page).
